title: Supplying source material and asking for structure

sections.skill: Supply source material and request structured output

questions.domain: Foundation 4: Asking for what you need
questions.prompt: Why paste the actual policy text and say "use only the text below"?

choices.text: It retrains the model on the policy
It steers the answer toward your material
It guarantees the answer is perfect

questions.correct_answer: It steers the answer toward your material
questions.intro: Two habits make results more grounded and easier to check. First, SUPPLY THE RELEVANT SOURCE MATERIAL: paste the actual policy, article, notes or data you want used, and say "use only the text below." That steers the answer toward your material instead of the tool's general patterns. Second, ask for STRUCTURED OUTPUT, such as a table with named columns or a list with a fixed set of fields, that you can scan quickly. A table of "Claim | Where in the text" is much easier to verify than a long paragraph. Supply only what is relevant; unrelated material can distract.

sections.skill: Match a claim to the sentence that supports it

questions.domain: Foundation 4: Asking for what you need
questions.prompt: Which sentence supports "It is closed Sundays"?
questions.correct_answer: Sentence 3
questions.intro: To check whether a summary used its source faithfully, take one CLAIM at a time and find the SENTENCE in the source that supports it. Source: "The library opens at 9 a.m. on weekdays. On Saturdays it opens at 10. It is closed Sundays." Claim: "It opens at 10 on Saturdays." Supported by sentence 2. Claim: "It opens at 9 every day." Not supported: sentence 1 says weekdays only. If no sentence supports a claim, or a sentence contradicts it, mark the claim.

sections.skill: Check that supplied material was used faithfully

questions.domain: Foundation 4: Asking for what you need
questions.prompt: An answer about a supplied policy includes a rule the policy never mentions. What happened?

choices.text: The policy must secretly contain it
The rule must be correct anyway
Supplied text always prevents outside facts

questions.correct_answer: The tool added outside information
questions.intro: Supplying material does not guarantee faithful use. A tool may still add outside facts, misread a table, or miss part of a long document. Asking it to quote or point to the exact sentence for each claim makes gaps visible. Structured output has limits too: a neat table can contain wrong values, and forcing information into fixed columns can drop important nuance, such as "only on weekdays." Check a few entries against the source, and include a "notes" column when exceptions matter.
questions.feedback: Supplying material does not guarantee faithful use.
